title: The free model on our own PC
scenario:
A small studio makes product shots for a paying client. It wants to stop paying per image and run FLUX.2 [klein] on its own PC with diffusers. Your teammate wrote the setup notes. You review them before the first client job.

Use the exhibit. The studio, the PC and the notes are made up for this case. The model names and licences are from the vendors' docs in October 2026.
exhibit:
SETUP NOTES (draft, made up)

  1  Model:     FLUX.2 [klein] 9B. "Open weights, so it's free
               for the client job."
  2  Download:  from_pretrained(...) for a FLUX repo fails with
               an access error (401). "The model must be broken."
  3  Speed-up:  swapped the default FLUX scheduler for one from
               an anime blog. Images now look smeared.
  4  Next step: put the PC behind a web page so the client's
               shoppers can type their own prompts. "Same as the
               API, just cheaper."

questions.prompt: Note 1 picks FLUX.2 [klein] 9B for the paid client job. What should change?

options.text: Nothing: open weights are always free to use for any kind of work
options.explanation: Open weights come with a licence. The BFL docs list [klein] 9B under the FLUX Non-Commercial License.

options.text: Use [klein] 4B (Apache 2.0), or check the 9B licence before any client work
options.explanation: Right. The BFL docs list 4B under Apache 2.0 and 9B under the FLUX Non-Commercial License. A non-commercial name means stop and check.

options.text: Use the 9B Base model instead, since Base models have no licence
options.explanation: The BFL docs list the 9B Base under the same FLUX Non-Commercial License.

options.text: Keep 9B but run it offline, since a licence only covers online use
options.explanation: Running offline does not change the licence on the weights.

questions.prompt: Note 2: the FLUX download fails with an access error. What is the likely fix?

options.text: Rename the model folder so the library stops checking access
options.explanation: Some FLUX downloads are gated: access needs an account. Renaming a folder does not give access.

options.text: Switch to the BFL API, because gated models cannot be run locally
options.explanation: Gated models can run locally. The quickstart only says you need an account to use them.

options.text: Log in with a Hugging Face account, which gated models like Flux need
options.explanation: Right. The diffusers quickstart says to have a Hugging Face account to use gated models like Flux.

options.text: Reinstall diffusers, because an access error means a broken install
options.explanation: An access error on a gated repo points to the account, not to the library.

questions.prompt: Note 3: after the scheduler swap, images look smeared. What do the diffusers docs advise?

options.text: Keep FLUX's default scheduler unless you test a compatible one on purpose
options.explanation: Right. Diffusers says FLUX models ship a default scheduler: keep it unless you are intentionally experimenting.

options.text: Swap the VAE too, because the scheduler and VAE must always match
options.explanation: The VAE encodes and decodes images. The change here was the scheduler.

options.text: Raise the guidance until the smears go away, then keep the new one
options.explanation: Guidance changes how closely the prompt is followed. The swapped scheduler is the cause.

options.text: Change the text encoder, because it decides how much noise to remove
options.explanation: Diffusers says the scheduler tells the denoising loop how much noise to remove at each step.

questions.prompt: Note 4 opens the PC to the public. What is wrong with "same as the API"?

options.text: Nothing: every local pipeline runs the same checks as the vendor's API
options.explanation: On your own machine you get only what the pipeline includes. The FLUX.2 parts list has no safety checker.

options.text: The local pipeline lists no safety checker; add checks or use an API
options.explanation: Right. Diffusers says newer models such as Qwen-Image do not have its checker, and the FLUX.2 parts list has none. For Stable Diffusion, diffusers strongly recommends keeping the safety filter in public-facing use.

options.text: Local images always carry a SynthID watermark, so shoppers are safe
options.explanation: Google's page says Gemini images include SynthID. The FLUX.2 pipeline lists no watermark step.

options.text: The only issue is speed; public prompts are fine once the PC is fast
options.explanation: Speed matters, but the bigger gap is safety: no checker in the pipeline for public prompts.
